commentary: A small dip for the pot, down £126. A hotter-than-expected US inflation reading (October CPI +0.4% against 0.3% expected) and Fed Governor Waller backing a rate rise in December pushed Wall Street lower: the S&P 500 fell 0.4% and the Nasdaq 0.7%, with tech the weakest sector. NVIDIA dropped 5.5% (about £172), down 9.6% in two sessions, on the board probe into CEO Jensen Huang and a report of $7.5bn of chips reaching China through a businesswoman; Microsoft fell 2.2% (about £61). Amazon rose 1.5% (about £96). In London the FTSE 100 slipped 0.3% to 10,751.59; Shell fell 2.1% (about £65) as oil dropped on hopes the US-Iran war is ending, and the gold fund lost 1.6% (about £107), while the global tracker VWRP added 0.4% (about £132) and HSBC 0.3%. The pound eased slightly to 1.3341 from 1.3360. Cash is now the £45,147.68 shown on AJ Bell this afternoon, £7.21 below the calculated figure used until yesterday.
